column8: Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 reference only: the standard handbook's words for the series idea already in the store (H5-034, H4-075's 10-out-of-10); sources spine row 2's arithmetic, adds no new claim, and NIST is not investing literature, so a footnote at most.
Mon 16 Nov: a second handbook for the same rule; the card itself says one is enough; if ever cited, a textbook, never a requirement (its cover says do not cite as one).
Mon 16 Nov: restates spine row 2's 9.6% (H1-081, H6-010, H5-034); the only new line is prose advice (about 1 time in 10 in prose, 9.6% once), which travels with H1-081.
Mon 16 Nov: the product rule's independence assumption is the hinge row 5 states as bounds; carry NIST's sentence as row 5's first clause if 2.3 needs it.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, strengthens spine row 2: structural reliability puts one issuer (perfect dependence) at a series' lower bound and ten independent issuers at its upper bound, an outside field the store lacked; equation read garbled, the sentence read clean.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, the sharpest strengthening of spine row 2 (one borrower is the best case, ten independent ones 9.56% against a 10% ceiling). Fix: say ten independent borrowers, never diversifying in general (real defaults correlate and sit lower, row 19); call 10% an arithmetic ceiling, not a real portfolio; 95% of the way and Boole's bound are Keel arithmetic, Boole not read at source; one number at most beside 9.6%.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.0 and 3a, the case's high degree of certainty read for the set: engineers apportion a target down a series by the nth root, so ten that must hold 99% together need 99.9% each; inverse form of H5-034 and H6-010, adds the handbook's practice; direction only (equal apportionment is the crudest method).

Mon 16 Nov: series against parallel explains Q8a-026 and H5-036 (spare money in the same issuer); its one new clause travels with Q8a-026: the extra Treasuries cover low rates, not the issuer; say the extra Treasuries, never backstop (WORDS).

Mon 16 Nov: 2.2, the fund rungs (net asset value, TNA Note 2) are the chain's softest links, not the issuer. Fix: the use says only as sure as the least sure rung, the handbook says weaker than it; 2.2 chose IBTR for 2037 over a listed Feb-2036 bond (SKELETON 2.2, NUMBERS 8m), so never say T-bonds wherever WInS listed them; size it with the 0.5% cut (Q3c, about 0.27%).

Mon 16 Nov: same paper and page as Q14a-026; overrating that all ten are paid and underrating that one breaks are one bias; the complex-system sentence may join Q14a-026's quote as the reason spine row 2 lands.
Mon 16 Nov: a two-year toy at 10% hazards with the same shape as Gibson's real basket; Li's copula carries 2008 baggage for a finance judge, so the Fed paper carries the point.
Mon 16 Nov: one issuer is one event restates H1-081; Li's limiting case is the end Gibson's 0.9 column approaches.
Mon 16 Nov: ten names at 1% is the aha's exact shape, but the one-name 60bp is Keel's approximation, while Gibson's sum is printed; keep for questions, one market source in the report.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, the honest cost of spine row 2 in prices: one issuer lowers the chance any payment breaks and raises the chance many break together (5th-to-default 0 to 31bp); evidence behind row 35's one sentence, not prose of its own.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, strengthens spine row 2 with outside proof from a Fed Board paper: a first-default basket costs the sum of its names when independent (352bp, the five spreads sum exactly) and nears the riskiest name as they move together (168 against 146bp); one clause or a footnote, shape only (2004 names).
Mon 16 Nov: both bounds in words from a working paper; quote it beside row 15 only if that clause needs words; one citation is enough.

Mon 16 Nov: an emerging-market model (default at the earlier of company and sovereign); S&P's own criteria allow ratings above the sovereign, so never state it as a rule for US companies; row 33 carries the point that other issuers would not escape.
Mon 16 Nov: the S&P table behind row 19; cite it once there.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, strengthens spine row 2: the hypothetical 99% each is about an AA company, and ten of them, one per payment, miss about 9 in 100 histories (Keel arithmetic on S&P 1981-2024); say if their defaults were independent, and a default is not a total loss.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, strengthens spine row 2 by joining its halves: investment-grade defaults came in 2008-09, a downturn a writer's income can fall in, so corporate rungs could add to her career risk (IPS l.9). Fix: can, never would or in the same years (card Q50 wording); 2009 only, since 2020 does not support the career link (Q56); one-year global rates.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e, answers the strongest objection to spine row 2 (a diversified corporate term fund). Fix: the plan's own fund rungs pay net asset value too, so the contrast is credit losses, never a known amount against a fixed one; escrow lists (Q54) bar every fund, Laura's iBond funds included, so never cite them here; never say it would lose money.
Mon 16 Nov: one more rule that lifts its cap for the government, the message of Q63-037 to Q63-043; a 30-day on-demand buffer, analogy only.
Mon 16 Nov: same message as row 24 (money owed at par sits with the government); payable on demand and crypto-adjacent, a weaker fit; one outside parallel is enough.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3, a strikingly dissimilar parallel for spine row 2: the fund behind every insured US deposit may by law hold only US obligations, so 89.55% in one issuer reads as deliberate; one clause at most, on-demand money not dated; Q8b-024 holds only the insurance limit.
Mon 16 Nov: a statute funding money owed with Treasuries matched to need restates H3-069 (26 U.S.C. 130(d), placed in 3a); one statute is enough.
Mon 16 Nov: a surety-bond requirement, not a ban; same message as row 24.
Mon 16 Nov: store, second case for row 31's rule if needed: the median central bank holds no corporate credit; reserves serve policy needs, not dated payments, so analogy only.
Mon 16 Nov: matching a portfolio to a group of liabilities is in the store at stronger sources (Leibowitz, Q1c-029); tranching itself was rejected (H5-078).

Mon 16 Nov: client knowledge for questions (2.3 or 3d): the matching issuer is the government of the promise's currency, so US Treasuries for US-dollar payments to a Taiwan residency; the case and WInS fixed the choice; never a reason to hold Taiwan dollars.

Mon 16 Nov: store, beside row 34: in the crisis reserve managers cut non-guaranteed bonds (53.6%) far more than long AAA government bonds (8.9%); 56 respondents, shares of banks not of money; the plan starts where they moved.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 or 3e, strengthens spine row 2 by bounding it: UK annuity writers diversify credit because they hold capital and pool many lives; with nothing behind each promise but the extra Treasuries, Laura sits with escrows; answers insurers hold corporates before a judge asks; the rule is Keel's synthesis.
Mon 16 Nov: the regulator's sentence (the spread table assumes a well-diversified pool) is row 31's reason; one argument, cite beside row 31.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e, the honest limit's price: S&P says a sovereign default brings a significant rise in nonsovereign defaults, so other issuers would not escape the one shared risk; mostly emerging-market cases, no US test; gives up little is Keel's reading.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3's turn or 3e: on the 2011 downgrade Treasury yields fell while the S&P 500 fell 6.8%. Fix: a downgrade, not a missed payment, so never that a default would raise Treasury prices; cite the 5- and 10-year only (the first maturity is cut off); H1-033 and Q15-027 already hold the yields, the new part is shares falling the same day.

Mon 16 Nov: 3e's one plain sentence of the shared risk; restates H1-081 and IPS l.17. Fix: its idea says all ten are late together, the delay reading its own guard forbids as fact; say paid late or missed together, with 1979 and prices as how it has gone, not a promise.

Mon 16 Nov: 2.3 placement: lead with the turn, 9.6% once, one outside example (row 15 or row 24), then diversify Laura; restates the card's verdict; a credit-trained judge finds the arithmetic obvious, the turn to her career stays new.
